page: PDF 177 / printed 157 (legend and caption); also PDF 176 / printed 156 and PDF 181 / printed 161
figure: FIG 9.1 legend, entry 'Two-way HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s'
issue: The legend label 'Two-way HDR' is ambiguous in a way that changes the answer by 2×, and the same 40 GB/s assumption is given three different names in the book (legend 'Two-way', p.156 'two-rank', p.161 '2 HDR rails/ports per node').
evidence: 'Two-way' most naturally reads as a bidirectional aggregate (send + receive on one link). Under that reading the ring moves 245 GB sent per rank at 20 GB/s per direction = 12.25 s, not the 6.1 s printed in the figure subtitle, the caption, and printed p.156. The book's own framing elsewhere is explicitly per-direction: printed p.161 states '490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time', i.e. 245 GB sent at 450 GB/s directional, and FIG 9.1's NVLink entry is labelled 'directional peak 450 GB/s'. The HDR entry is the only one whose directionality is unspecified, and it is the one whose label admits a 2× misreading.
acceptance_test: Choose one unambiguous descriptor for the 40 GB/s assumption and use it identically in the FIG 9.1 legend, the FIG 9.1 caption, printed p.156, and printed p.161. Recommended: 'HDR, 2 rails/node, assumed effective 40 GB/s per direction'. The words 'per direction' must appear in the legend entry so that the 245 GB / 40 GB/s = 6.125 s arithmetic is forced by the label rather than inferred.

issue: The figure says 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' and shows R0→R1→R2→R3→R0, but it does not show which 2 B chunk each rank sends in each round. For a reader trying to reconstruct the ring algorithm, the diagram shows the neighbor order but not the chunk rotation that makes reduce-scatter and all-gather work.
evidence: Figure text: 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' with R0→R1→R2→R3→R0. Below: 'Each round sends one 2 B chunk to the next rank.' The figure does not label the chunks (e.g., chunk 0, chunk 1, chunk 2, chunk 3) or show which chunk moves in round 1, 2, 3. The caption says 'Reduce-scatter leaves one reduced element per rank; all-gather then replicates the already-reduced fragments', but the chunk rotation is left implicit.
acceptance_test: Either add small chunk labels (0/1/2/3) to the ring arrows or add one sentence to the caption: 'In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N; the same rotation is used in both phases.'

figure: FIG 9.2 subtitle: 'Four ranks; four FP16 elements per input (6 B/rank).'
issue: The parenthetical states the input size as 6 B/rank, but four FP16 elements are 8 B/rank; 6 B is the per-phase sent volume, not the input size. As written the figure's own headline number is wrong.
evidence: Four FP16 elements × 2 B = 8 B per rank of input. The figure body correctly shows '6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' per phase and 'Per rank: 12 B sent + 12 B received = 24 B endpoint total', and the caption says 'each rank sends 12 B and receives 12 B across both phases'. 12 B sent / 8 B input = 1.5 = 2(N−1)/N at N=4, which is the same factor FIG 9.1 uses at N=8 (1.75). If the input really were 6 B, the ratio would be 2.0, contradicting both figures. The parenthetical is attached to 'per input', so the natural reading is input size.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the subtitle as 'Four ranks; four FP16 elements per input (8 B/rank); 6 B sent + 6 B received per rank per phase' and confirm that 8 B input → 12 B sent → 1.5× is stated or derivable on the page. Re-check that no other caption or prose in Chapter 9 repeats the '6 B/rank' input figure.

figure: FIG 9.2 phase annotations ('3 neighbor rounds / 6 B sent + 6 B received/rank')
issue: '3 neighbor rounds' can be misread as '3 neighbors', but a four-rank ring has exactly two distinct neighbors per rank; the quantity being counted is rounds (steps), not neighbors.
evidence: The figure's own ring sub-diagram shows R0→R1→R2→R3→R0, i.e. two neighbors per rank. The correct count is 3 rounds (N−1 steps) per phase, each moving one 2 B chunk, as the separate note 'Each rank sends one 2 B chunk to the next rank' states.
acceptance_test: Change both phase annotations to '3 rounds (one 2 B chunk per round)' or '3 steps × 2 B = 6 B sent per rank', so that rounds and neighbors are not conflated.

figure: FIG 9.2 reduce-scatter row (Rank 0 → [10], Rank 1 → [20], Rank 2 → [-10], Rank 3 → [0])
issue: The figure asserts a specific chunk→rank ownership (rank r ends with reduced chunk r) without stating the chunk-flow convention, and the most commonly taught forward-flow convention yields rank r → chunk r+1. An expert reader who knows that convention will read the figure as wrong rather than as a convention choice.
evidence: With the textbook convention 'at step 0 rank r forwards its own chunk r to its successor', chunk j starts at rank j and completes at rank j−1, so rank r would hold chunk r+1 (rank 0 → 20, rank 1 → −10, rank 2 → 0, rank 3 → 10). The figure's assignment is nevertheless achievable — it corresponds to the variant where rank r forwards chunk r−1 first, so chunk j starts at rank j+1 and completes at rank j — but the figure shows only the neighbour order, not the chunk flow, so the reader cannot tell which convention is in force.
acceptance_test: Add one clause to the caption or the figure, e.g. 'chunk j is first forwarded by rank j+1, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r', or annotate the ring sub-diagram with the chunk index in flight. Confirm that the stated convention reproduces the four reduce-scatter outputs shown.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The figure's right-hand path places 'Plugin: MPI or OFI' under '3 Device runtime plus transport', while the bottom note says 'GPU-aware MPI can carry payload too; MPI is not CPU-only.' The diagram therefore shows MPI in two different roles (setup/control and transport/plugin) without visually distinguishing those roles.

Right path under '3 Device runtime plus transport': 'SYCL / Level Zero path / Plugin: MPI or OFI / Actual path depends on build'. Bottom note: 'GPU-aware MPI can carry payload too; MPI is not CPU-only.' Caption: 'Dashed setup connections do not imply that MPI carries the collective payload; GPU-aware MPI is also a possible payload implementation.' The figure uses the same word 'MPI' for setup and for a possible transport/plugin without a visual or textual role distinction.
acceptance_test: Either label the right-path MPI entry as 'MPI transport (payload-capable)' or add a caption sentence: 'MPI appears in two roles: setup/rendezvous (dashed) and, in some builds, payload transport (solid); the figure does not imply they are the same path.'

figure: FIG 9.3, dashed red 'Control / setup' path vs. the 'Launcher, rank/device mapping, rendezvous' box
issue: The horizontal run of the dashed control path sits immediately above the launcher box's top border, so at print size the dashed red rule and the box's solid grey rule read as one double line and the control path appears to bypass the launcher rather than pass through it.

The figure's semantic claim is that the launcher performs the setup for both backends, which requires the dashed path to visibly terminate on the box.

Re-render at 150 dpi and confirm the two rules are separable at print size.

page: PDF 181 / printed 161 (equation); FIG 9.1 on PDF 177 / printed 157; prose on PDF 176 / printed 156
figure: FIG 9.1 (model) vs. the ring-latency equation in §9.3
issue: The ring-latency equation in §9.3 omits the factor of 2 for the two phases of an all-reduce, so its own printed substitution does not produce the printed result, and the equation contradicts the model drawn in FIG 9.1 and the prose on printed p.156.
evidence: Printed on p.161: 'T_ring ≈ (N−1)/N · M/R_eff ≈ 7/8 · 140 GB / 40 GB/s ≈ 6.1 s'. Substitution: 7/8 = 0.875; 140/40 = 3.5; 0.875 × 3.5 = 3.06 s — a factor of 2 short of the printed 6.1 s. The correct ring all-reduce critical path is 2(N−1)/N · M/R_eff = 1.75 × 140/40 = 6.125 s, which is exactly the model drawn in FIG 9.1 ('sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes', '140 GB tensor (245 GB sent at 1.75×)', 'HDR 6,125 ms') and the prose on printed p.156 ('the eight-rank ring on 8×3 instead sends 245 GB per rank: about 0.54 s at the H100 directional peak, 6.1 s at an assumed effective ... 40 GB/s'). FIG 9.2 independently confirms the 2(N−1)/N form: 12 B sent for a 4-element FP16 input = 1.5× = 2(N−1)/N at N=4. The finding holds even if a '2' is present in the source formula, because the printed substitution '7/8 · 140 GB / 40 GB/s' omits it.
acceptance_test: In the source, change the equation to 'T_ring ≈ 2(N−1)/N · M/R_eff ≈ 2 × 7/8 × 140 GB / 40 GB/s ≈ 6.1 s' (equivalently '1.75 × 140 GB / 40 GB/s'), and add a clause naming the two phases ('reduce-scatter + all-gather'). Confirm that the printed 6.1 s, FIG 9.1's 245 GB / 6,125 ms, FIG 9.1's caption '6.1 s', and printed p.156's '6.1 s' all agree, then re-run the numeric regression gate over Chapter 9.

figure: Figure 10.1, caption (Panel B / 'GPU counts and layer ranges schematic' clause)
issue: Caption states 'the canonical host is 8×H100 and the canonical 70B has 8 layers'. A 70B model with 8 layers is impossible under the book's own canonical KV figure, and the figure itself draws 24 layers (1–8, 9–16, 17–24), not 8.
evidence: Independent rederivation from the book's own canonical: FP16 full-MHA KV = 2.62 MB/token = n_layers × 4 × hidden bytes. With hidden = 8192: 2.62e6 / (4 × 8192) = 79.95 ≈ 80 layers. An 8-layer reading would require hidden ≈ 81,875, which no architecture has. Standard 70B (Llama-2-70B class, hidden 8192) has 80 layers. The drawn ranges (1–24 across three GPUs) also contradict '8 layers' even allowing for the 'schematic' disclaimer, which covers GPU counts and ranges, not the layer-count claim itself. Most likely a dropped zero (8 → 80).
root_cause: Typo in Fig 10.1 caption layer count; possibly propagated if the canonical model definition elsewhere repeats it.
correction: Change caption to 'the canonical 70B has 80 layers' (or whatever the canonical model definition in Ch 2/3 states), keeping the 'GPU counts and layer ranges schematic' disclaimer.
acceptance_test: Caption layer count equals the canonical model's layer count used for all KV and pipeline arithmetic elsewhere in the book; grep all occurrences of '8 layers' vs '80 layers' for the canonical 70B. If any other location also says 8 layers, escalate to P0 and fix all anchors.

issue: Panel A's weight bar is drawn as one continuous blue bar split at the GPU boundary and labeled 'W1' (over GPU 0) and 'W2' (over GPU 1). As drawn, the natural reading is 'GPU 0 holds matrix W1, GPU 1 holds matrix W2' — i.e. matrix-per-GPU placement, which is NOT tensor parallelism. Under TP both GPUs hold shards of the SAME matrix. The caption ('TP shards one layer's weights across GPUs') disambiguates in prose, but the figure alone licenses the wrong mental model, and the book elsewhere distinguishes TP from EP ('EP reuses the same machinery'), so the confusion is not harmless.
evidence: Rendered panel A: a single hatched bar spanning both GPU boxes, with 'W1' centered over GPU 0 and 'W2' centered over GPU 1, and no label identifying the parent matrix. Caption: 'TP shards one layer's weights across GPUs (activations replicated; partial sums all-reduced every layer)'. Panel title: 'splits one layer's weights'.
acceptance_test: Panel A's bar must be labeled as one matrix divided into shards — e.g. a brace over the bar reading 'one layer's weight matrix W' with the halves labeled 'shard 1 (GPU 0)' / 'shard 2 (GPU 1)' or 'W[:, :h]' / 'W[:, h:]' — so that no reader can read the drawing as 'GPU 0 holds W1, GPU 1 holds W2'. Re-render and confirm the intended reading is forced by the labels alone, without the caption.

issue: The in-figure legend glosses blue as 'compute', but the only blue element in the figure is the static weight matrix in panel A. The caption glosses the same color differently: 'the figure color code (blue = weights · orange = GPU · green = data · red = comms)'. A reader who trusts the legend will read the blue bar as compute work rather than a parameter, which inverts the meaning of the panel (the thing being split is data, not compute).
evidence: Rendered legend row: 'compute (blue) | GPU (orange) | data (green) | comms (red)'. Caption: 'the figure color code (blue = weights · orange = GPU · green = data · red = comms)'. Panel A's blue hatched bar is labeled W1/W2 (weights).
acceptance_test: The legend entry and the caption gloss must use the same word for blue — 'weights (blue)' in both places — or the blue element must be relabeled so that 'compute' is not attached to a static parameter. Verify by reading only the figure and only the caption: both must yield the same mapping.

issue: Grayscale distinguishability is weaker than the caption's 'Grayscale note' claims. The caption asserts the color code is 'redundant, not load-bearing' because each box carries a text label — true for the GPU boxes, but the legend itself becomes four indistinguishable gray squares in grayscale, and the two semantic categories that use hatch texture (weights = blue diagonal hatch in panel A; data = green diagonal hatch in panel C) use the SAME hatch angle, so a grayscale reader sees one texture standing for two different categories. The legend swatches are solid fills and do not reproduce the hatch patterns used in the panels.
evidence: Rendered panels: panel A's weight bar uses diagonal hatching; panel C's 'batch shard A/B' bars use diagonal hatching; the GPU boxes use cross-hatching. Legend swatches are solid color squares with no texture.
acceptance_test: Render in grayscale and confirm (a) the weights bar and the batch-shard bars are distinguishable by hatch pattern alone (e.g. diagonal vs horizontal vs cross-hatch), and (b) each legend swatch reproduces the pattern used in the panels rather than a solid fill.

issue: The PP row's 'Replicates' cell reads 'hidden states', but hidden states are exactly what the same row's 'Communicates' column, the adjacent prose, and Fig 10.1 all treat as *transferred* point-to-point at stage boundaries — not replicated. Listing the same object as both replicated and communicated is either wrong or undefined.
evidence: Same table row: Communicates = 'hidden states → P2P (stage boundaries only)'. Same page prose: 'hidden states cross stage boundaries point-to-point'. Fig 10.1 panel B label: 'activations → P2P at stage boundaries'. Benign-interpretation challenge: the only defensible reading is 'hidden states remain unsharded (full tensors)', but the column header is literally 'Replicates', which conventionally means multiple copies; each stage holds a *different* tensor (layer-8 output vs layer-16 output), so nothing is copied.
root_cause: Column cell conflates 'not partitioned' with 'replicated', or duplicates the Communicates content.
correction: Replace the cell with what PP actually replicates (e.g., '— (full hidden state passes through unsharded)' or 'nothing' with a one-line footnote defining the column), or redefine the column header so 'replicates' ≠ 'transfers'. Table, Fig 10.1, and prose must then agree.
acceptance_test: For each of the five rows, the 'Replicates' cell names an object that exists in multiple copies on multiple devices and does not also appear in that row's 'Communicates' cell unless the duplication is explicitly explained; Fig 10.1 caption's 'replication is described where it exists' list remains accurate.
